channel.title: Mini Diarium Blog
channel.description: Static articles about encrypted journals, private diary apps, offline journaling, and local-first software.

item.title: Notion Alternative for Private Journaling
item.description: Notion stores journal entries on its servers, where AI features can read them. Here is what changes moving journaling to an encrypted, local-only app instead.

item.title: Obsidian Alternative for Journal Writing
item.description: Obsidian has no built-in encryption: vault files sit as plain Markdown on disk. For journal writing that needs encryption at rest, here is a direct comparison.

item.title: Standard Notes Alternative for Encrypted Journaling
item.description: Looking for a Standard Notes alternative for private journaling? Mini Diarium stores everything locally with AES-256-GCM and no sync service or server dependency.

item.title: Desktop Diary Apps: What to Look for in 2026
item.description: A desktop diary app should store entries locally, encrypt them at rest, and work without a network connection. Here is what matters and what to check.

item.title: How to Choose a Private Journal App in 2026
item.description: A private journal app should encrypt entries at rest, work fully offline, avoid telemetry, and give you a portable export. Here is a practical checklist for evaluating one.

item.title: What Is an Encrypted Diary? Why Encryption at Rest Matters
item.description: An encrypted diary encrypts entries before they are written to disk. It is not the same as a password-protected app. Here is what the term actually means and why it matters for private journaling.

item.title: Can AI Access Your Journal? Cloud Storage and the Case for Local
item.description: Cloud journaling apps can expose your entries to AI training, policy updates, or server-side analysis. An offline, local-first journal provides a structural guarantee that cloud privacy settings cannot match.

item.title: Mini Diary Alternative in 2026: A Maintained, Encrypted Successor
item.description: Mini Diary went unmaintained. Mini Diarium is its successor, rebuilt with AES-256-GCM encryption, key file auth, and direct import from Mini Diary JSON. Same philosophy, stronger guarantees.

item.title: Journal App Without Cloud: What Actually Matters
item.description: A journal app without cloud dependency should keep entries local, work offline, encrypt writing before storage, and make export straightforward when you want full control.

item.title: Day One Alternative for Private Offline Journaling
item.description: Looking for a Day One alternative? The right replacement should keep journal entries local, work offline, support import and export, and make long-term ownership clearer.

item.title: Encrypted Journal vs. Cloud Notes: Why Architecture Decides Who Owns Your Writing
item.description: An encrypted journal app stores entries locally and encrypts before disk. Cloud apps store plaintext on servers. The architecture, not a privacy setting, decides who can read your writing.

item.title: Offline Journal That You Own: Portability, Privacy, and No Cloud Strings
item.description: Owning your journal means keeping entries local, exporting them in open formats, and never depending on a service to access your own writing. Here's what that requires.

item.title: Private Diary App for Desktop: 5 Things Cloud Apps Can't Promise
item.description: A private diary app for desktop should encrypt entries at rest, work fully offline, and give you an exit path. Here's the checklist for evaluating one.

item.title: Local-First Journaling Means You Keep the Exit Door Open
item.description: Local-first journaling is not only about privacy. It is also about durability, portability, and keeping your encrypted journal exportable when your tooling changes.

item.title: Why an Offline Journal Protects More Than Just Your Privacy
item.description: An offline journal can't sync your entries to a server or share them with AI. That's not a setting. It's the absence of network code. Here's why architecture outlasts privacy policies.

item.title: Why Mini Diarium Exists
item.description: Mini Diarium exists because private journaling software needed a maintained Mini Diary successor, rebuilt as an encrypted offline journal with a modern stack.
